text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovak companies may soon have problems planning longer-term investment activities due to the turbulent situation on local money market which is preventing them from obtaining financial sources, analysts said.
- Consumer prices in May rose 0.1 percent month-on-month, while the annual inflation rate stood at 6.1 percent.
- Short-term interbank rates on Tuesday continued to trade at levels above 30 percent.

- Import deposits, imposed both by the Czech Republic and Slovakia, will effect about 24.1 percent of Bratislava's exports to the Czech Republic and should total some 24.1 billion crowns. The Slovak deposit measure will affect some 38.1 percent, or 31.3 billion crowns, of imports from the Czech Republic.

PRAVDA - All major opposition parties have rejected Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's invitation to start round table negotiations saying they would not hold any talks with Meciar unless Interior Minister Gustav Krajci is dismissed.

- Parliamentary deputy of the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL), Jan Sopko, warned that state-run Slovak Railways (ZRS) was near financial collapse and called for the government to solve ZRS's critical situation.
SME - All parliamentary opposition parties will demand the dismissal of Minister Krajci at an extraordinary session of parliament on Thursday.
PRACA - The government on Tuesday said it still supported Krajci in his post.
- Slovak beer producers have welcomed the introduction of quotas on imports of Czech beer.

SLOVENSKA REPUBLIKA - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said Slovakia was still at the beginning of economic restructuring and that economic reforms have still not proceeded far enough to guarantee sustainable economic growth over the long term.
